The innermost ISO 7 Cleanroom Suite 115B, and the ISO 5 BSC E001314 within the Suite 115B were 
thoroughly cleaned and prepared before initiating the testing as per SOP 2.600.002 (Environmental Monitoring 
of the Clean Room Facility), and SOP 2.600.018 (Cleaning and Disinfecting Procedure for Microbiology). 
Furthermore, the BSC used throughout testing, E001314, was certified and approved by both the Engineering 
and Quality Assurance teams.

Upon review of the environmental monitoring results (Tables 2 and 3), no microbial growth was detected 
on surface samples or settling plates collected during either the processing or subculture testing days. 
However, two CFUs were observed on the left-hand personnel plate collected on the day of testing. These 
isolates were identified as Staphylococcus warneri and Staphylococcus pasteuri. Additionally, one CFU 
was recovered from the ISO 7 115A Buffer Room active air plate and identified as Micrococcus luteus. All 
other weekly active air and surface samples collected during the original processing and subculture date, 
showed no microbial growth. Therefore, although microbial growth was observed on a personnel 
monitoring plate on the day of processing and on an active air sample from the ISO 7 115A Buffer Room 
during the week of subculture, these isolates were not identical to those recovered from the sample under 
investigation.

JEsqueda , 9/30/2025, 4:15:53 PM
Environmental Monitoring Summary: Personnel sampling plate for analyst Muralidhar Reddy Bythatagari 
for the previous date, and following date of testing showed no microbial growth. 60 CFUs were observed 
on the Left Touch plate for analyst Muralidhar Reddy Bythatagari on the date of testing. Microbial 
identification is pending for the same. Settling Sampling plates and surface sampling plates for ISO 5 BSC 
1314 for the previous date, date of and following date of testing showed no microbial growth. The weekly 
Active Air Sampling for Anteroom & Buffer room for CR115 for the week of testing, performed by analyst 
Tamiru Kotisso 10 Dec 2025, exhibited 1 CFU on the plate in ISO 8 CR115, which was morphologically 
identified as Gram (+) cocci. No growth was observed during the weekly surface sampling performed in 
the week of testing.

During the interview with the analyst, they indicated that no obvious abnormalities or deviations in the 
testing procedure were observed. All the samples were thoroughly disinfected prior to testing. Moreover, 
The ISO 7 CR 115B, and the ISO 5 BSC 1314 within the ISO 7 CR 115B were thoroughly cleaned and 
prepared before initiating the testing as per SOP 2.600.002 (Environmental Monitoring of the Clean Room 
Facility), and SOP 2.600.018 (Cleaning and Disinfecting Procedure for Microbiology).

JEsqueda , 9/30/2025, 4:15:53 PM
Based on the findings outlined in the preceding sections, the Out-Of-Specification (OOS) result observed 
for the Environmental Monitoring (EM) Personnel Sampling plate may be attributed to a potential analyst 
error. No growth was observed on the personnel sampling plate for the analyst as well as on the ISO 5 
BSC 1314 Surface &/or Settling sampling plates for the following date of testing, suggesting that the 
contamination originating from the analyst was transient in nature and daily routine disinfection procedures 
were effective in eliminating the contamination. Although a previous trend has been noted in the analyst's 
EM data and corresponding preventive and corrective actions were addressed under CAPA C25-025, it is 
important to note that the earlier trend was observed at least two months prior to the current positive EM 
result. Therefore, the present result is considered an isolated event, and no additional corrective or 
preventive actions are deemed necessary at this time. However, the analyst will be monitored for any 
potential recurrence or emerging trends of contamination.

Surface Sampling was performed by analyst Muralidhar Bythatagari during ScanRDI changeover, in ISO 5 
BSC 1311 located in Suite 116A, on 16 Dec 2025 as per SOP 2.600.002 - Environmental Monitoring of the 
Cleanroom Facility.

To observe if the organisms identified, were transient in nature or recurring, personnel monitoring plates 
for the analyst Muralidhar Bythatagari, and ISO 5 BSC 1311 environmental monitoring plates, were 
bracketed to include date before testing and date after testing as detailed in Table 2 (please see attached). 
252907

JEsqueda , 9/30/2025, 4:15:53 PM
Environmental Monitoring Summary: Personnel sampling plate for analyst Muralidhar Bythatagari for the 
previous date, date of, and following date of testing showed no microbial growth. Settling Sampling plates 
for ISO 5 BSC 1311 for the previous date, date of and following date of testing showed no microbial 
growth either. Similarly, ISO 5 BSC surface sampling plate for the previous date and following date of 
testing exhibited no microbial growth. However, 2 CFUs were observed on Surface# 2 of ISO 5 BSC 1311 
for the date of testing. Microbial identification is pending for the same. The weekly Active Air Sampling for 
Anteroom & Buffer room for CR116 for the week of testing, performed by analyst SMO on 19 Dec 2025, 
exhibited 1 CFU on the plate in ISO 8 CR116. Microbial identification is currently ongoing for this. No 
growth was observed on the weekly surface sampling plates for CR 116 for the week of testing, performed 
on 19 Dec 2025.

During the interview with the analyst, they indicated that no obvious abnormalities or deviations in the 
testing procedure were observed. All the samples were thoroughly disinfected prior to testing. Moreover, 
The ISO 7 CR 116A, and the ISO 5 BSC 1311 within the ISO 7 CR 116A were thoroughly cleaned and 
prepared before initiating the testing as per SOP 2.600.002 (Environmental Monitoring of the Clean Room 
Facility), and SOP 2.600.018 (Cleaning and Disinfecting Procedure for Microbiology).

JEsqueda , 9/30/2025, 4:15:53 PM
Based on the findings outlined in the preceding sections, the Out-Of-Specification (OOS) result observed 
for the Environmental Monitoring (EM) Surface Sampling plate may be attributed to a potential analyst 
error. No growth was observed on the other three surface sampling plates for the ISO 5 BSC for that day 
of testing. Additionally, no growth was observed on the settling, surface and personnel sampling plates for 
the BSC for the following date of testing, suggesting that the contamination originating from the analyst 
was transient in nature and daily routine disinfection procedures were effective in eliminating the 
contamination. Although a previous trend has been noted in the analyst's EM data and corresponding 
preventive and corrective actions were addressed under CAPA C25-025, it is important to note that the 
earlier trend was observed at least two months prior to the current positive EM result. Therefore, the 
present result is considered an isolated event, and no additional corrective or preventive actions are 
deemed necessary at this time. However, the analyst will be monitored for any potential recurrence or 
emerging trends of contamination.
252907

During the interview with the analyst who processed the original sample, it was noted that a foreign object was observed in the media 
bottle during inspection. Based on this observation, it was hypothesized that the contamination may have resulted from the introduction of 
this foreign material, representing a potential source of inadvertent laboratory error during processing.

Given that the retest from the same lot yielded a passing result, and considering the prior observation of a foreign object in the media, the 
original failed result is attributed to inadvertent laboratory error. Additionally, historical data support this conclusion: the analyte 
Testosterone Cypionate (GSO) 100 mg/mL, 2 mL from the same client, Tailor Made Compounding (E14883), has been tested 31 times 
across different lot numbers, with all previous results passing.

Therefore, based on the observations and supporting data outlined above, the original result for ETX-260106-00561 is attributed to 
laboratory error, deemed invalid, and will be updated to “--”. The retest result for ETX-260121-0366 will be considered valid for this 
specific lot.

On 11 May 2026, the sample containers were received from the Sample Submissions team and brought into the Sterile 
Microbiology lab. Upon receipt, each sample container was sprayed with an acidified bleach disinfectant, placed into 
pre-disinfected bins, and allowed a 10-minute contact time. Following initial disinfection, the bins were transferred to the 
ISO 8 anteroom (Suite 115), where the container underwent a second disinfection using acidified bleach, again with a 
10-minute contact time. Subsequently, the containers were moved into the ISO 7 clean room (Suite 115B). Inside this 
cleanroom, the processing analyst, Guanchen Li, performed a final disinfection step, allowing an additional 10-minute 
contact time. Once fully disinfected, the containers were transferred into the ISO 5 BSC E001314. Inside the BSC, each 
container was aseptically opened, ensuring minimal exposure to the environment. The contents were then dispensed 
directly from the container into sterile canisters placed on a vacuum manifold for membrane filtration. However, from 
preliminary interview findings, a potential laboratory error was identified from the processing analyst.  While opening the 
small vials, the analyst reported experiencing difficulty in aseptically opening the individual vials. During such 
manipulation, the analyst pointed that unintentional contact between the vial rim and gloved fingers, vial caps, external 
vial surfaces, or other items within the BSC may have occurred. Media bottles were then transferred into incubators 
E001356 and E001357 to begin incubation.
261241

Upon identification of a potential laboratory error, and given that the sample is part of an ongoing stability 
study, additional retain samples from the same lot were retrieved in from retains at the same storage 
conditions and submitted for re-testing under submission ETX-260526-0557. The findings from this 
additional testing will be reviewed and addressed as part of the Phase II investigation.

On 11 May 2026, the sample containers were received from the Sample Submissions team and brought into the Sterile Microbiology lab. Upon receipt, 
each sample container was sprayed with an acidified bleach disinfectant, placed into pre-disinfected bins, and allowed a 10-minute contact time. 
Following initial disinfection, the bins were transferred to the ISO 8 anteroom (Suite 115), where the container underwent a second disinfection using 
acidified bleach, again with a 10-minute contact time. Subsequently, the containers were moved into the ISO 7 clean room (Suite 115B). Inside this 
cleanroom, the processing analyst, Guanchen Li, performed a final disinfection step, allowing an additional 10-minute contact time. Once fully 
disinfected, the containers were transferred into the ISO 5 BSC E001314. Inside the BSC, each container was aseptically opened, ensuring minimal 
exposure to the environment. The contents were then dispensed directly from the container into sterile canisters placed on a vacuum manifold for 
membrane filtration. However, from preliminary interview findings, a potential laboratory error was identified from the processing analyst.  While opening 
the small vials, the analyst reported experiencing difficulty in aseptically opening the individual vials. During such manipulation, the analyst pointed that 
unintentional contact between the vial rim and gloved fingers, vial caps, external vial surfaces, or other items within the BSC may have occurred. Media 
bottles were then transferred into incubators E001356 and E001357 to begin incubation.

The innermost ISO 7 Cleanroom Suite 115B, and the ISO 5 BSC E001314 within the Suite 115B were thoroughly 
cleaned and prepared before initiating the testing as per SOP 2.600.002 (Environmental Monitoring of the Clean Room 
Facility), and SOP 2.600.018 (Cleaning and Disinfecting Procedure for Microbiology). Furthermore, the BSC used 
throughout testing, E001314, was certified and approved by both the Engineering and Quality Assurance teams.

Upon analyzing the environmental monitoring results (Table 2), no microbial growth was observed in 
surface sampling, settling plates or personnel plate collected on the day of testing, as well as the day 
before and the day after testing. The weekly active air sampling showed one CFU on the ISO 8 (Suite 
115) plate (identified as Micrococcus luteus) for the week after testing. No growth was observed on the 
weekly surface sampling from the week after testing. All other environmental monitoring plates from the 
cleanroom sampling were negative for microbial growth.

It is important to note that all processing activities were performed within ISO 5 biological safety cabinet 
(BSC) E001314, located in the innermost ISO 7 cleanroom (Room 115B). Environmental monitoring 
collected from BSC on the day of processing—including surface contact plates, settling plates, and 
personnel monitoring—demonstrated no microbial growth. These results indicate that the cleanroom and 
primary engineering controls were operating within validated specifications at the time of processing. 
Accordingly, based on the absence of detectable environmental contamination and the controlled 
processing conditions, the cleanroom environment is not considered a likely source of contamination for 
the sample.

Tables 2 and 3 present the environmental monitoring results for sample ETX-260615-0044. Environmental monitoring (EM) plates were 
incubated for a minimum of 48 hours at 30–35°C, followed by no less than five additional days at 20–25°C, in accordance with SOP 
2.600.002 (Environmental Monitoring of the Cleanroom Facility).

Review of the environmental monitoring data showed no microbial growth in personnel monitoring samples (left and right touch), surface 
sampling, or settling plates associated with both the processing analyst DT and the changeover analyst CGS.

The microbial recoveries identified during environmental monitoring are not considered to have impacted the sterility test results. All 
product-contact activities, including pre-labeling, filtration, and changeover, were performed within certified ISO 5 biological safety 
cabinets located inside ISO 7 buffer rooms (Suites 115A and 116A), which provide a significantly higher level of environmental control 
than the ISO 8 anterooms where the air recoveries were detected. Environmental monitoring performed on the date of testing 
demonstrated no microbial growth in personnel monitoring samples, ISO 5 surface samples, or ISO 5 settling plates associated with 
either processing or changeover activities. In addition, the cleanroom suites operate under a positive-pressure airflow design that directs 
air from the cleaner ISO 7 areas outward toward the ISO 8 anterooms, minimizing the potential for contamination migration from the ISO 
8 areas into the critical processing environments.

Furthermore, the organisms recovered from the ISO 8 active air samples were identified as Gram-positive cocci, whereas the 
microorganisms detected in the ScanRDI test sample exhibited a rod-shaped morphology. This difference in morphology demonstrates 
that the environmental monitoring recoveries are not consistent with the microorganisms detected in the sample. The only rod-shaped 
environmental recovery observed was a single CFU from a floor surface sample in ISO 7 Suite 116B, an area separate from the ISO 5 
processing environment, and no corresponding growth was detected on personnel, ISO 5 surface, or settling plates. When considered 
alongside the satisfactory cleaning and disinfection performed prior to use, the absence of contamination in critical environmental 
monitoring locations, and the negative results obtained for all other samples processed on the same day, the available evidence 
supports the conclusion that the microbial growth detected in the ISO 8 areas did not contribute to or impact the positive ScanRDI result

Based on the cumulative evidence, including environmental monitoring data, cleaning and disinfection records, sample history, and 
batch processing review, there is no indication that the positive result was caused by reagents, materials, environmental conditions, 
procedural deficiencies, or analyst error. Furthermore, the colony morphology of the microorganisms recovered from the cleanroom 
environment differed from that of the microorganism isolated from the test sample, indicating that the environmental monitoring 
recoveries and the test sample contamination represent separate and unrelated events. Accordingly, laboratory error is considered 
unlikely, and the original test result is determined to be valid.
261414

Upon review of the environmental monitoring (EM) results associated with the processing and aliquoting activities, 
limited microbial recovery was observed during personnel and settling plate monitoring. During the processing 
step, 1 CFU was recovered from Settling Plate 2 on the day after testing. The isolate was submitted for microbial 
identification under Sample ID ETX-260702-0300 and was identified as Staphylococcus warneri. During the 
aliquoting step, 4 CFUs were recovered from the analyst's left-touch personnel monitoring plate on the day prior to 
testing. The isolate was submitted for microbial identification under Sample ID ETX-260706-0280 and was 
identified as Bacillus paralicheniformis.The analysts involved in the activities confirmed full adherence to all 
applicable cleaning, disinfection, and aseptic processing procedures as defined in SOP 2.600.018, Cleaning and 
Disinfecting Procedure for Microbiology, SOP 2.600.059, Celsis Sterility Testing, and SOP 2.600.008,  USP <71>
/EP 2.6.1 Sterility Test.

Review of routine environmental monitoring data identified additional low-level microbial recovery within the 
surrounding ISO 8 areas. During weekly active air monitoring, 2 CFUs were detected in ISO 8 Room 115. The 
isolate was submitted for microbial identification under Sample ID ETX-260615-0432 and was identified as 
Staphylococcus epidermidis. In the week preceding the aliquoting activity, weekly active air monitoring detected 3 
CFUs in CR143 Section II (ISO 8) and 11 CFUs in CR142 (ISO 8). The isolates were submitted for microbial 
identification under Sample IDs ETX-260706-0305 and ETX-260706-0300. Identifications for ETX-260706-0305 
included Micrococcus luteus, Staphylococcus haemolyticus, and Auricoccus indicus, while isolates recovered 
under ETX-260706-0300 were identified as Micrococcus luteus, Staphylococcus capitis, and Tremateia 
guiyangensis.
261500

While sporadic microbial recovery was observed during routine environmental monitoring, it is important to 
note that the microorganisms identified were recovered primarily from the surrounding ISO 8 background 
environment. The processing and aliquoting operations were conducted exclusively within a qualified ISO 5 
BSC located in innermost ISO 7 Room (115B) and middle buffer ISO 7 Room (CR144) respectively, which 
provides a substantially higher level of environmental control than the surrounding room. Importantly, 
environmental monitoring results from the critical work area, including work surfaces and analyst glove 
monitoring, did not demonstrate contamination during the execution of the activities.

The innermost ISO 7 Clean-room Suite 114B, and the ISO 5 BSC E001316 within the Suite 114B were thoroughly cleaned and prepared before 
initiating the testing as per SOP 2.600.002 (Environmental Monitoring of the Clean Room Facility), and SOP 2.600.018 (Cleaning and 
Disinfecting Procedure for Microbiology). Furthermore, the BSC used for the testing, E001316, was certified and approved by the Engineering 
and Quality Assurance teams.

Tables 3-6 (see attached) presents the environmental monitoring results. The environmental monitoring (EM) plates were incubated for no less than 48 
hours at 30-35°C and no less than an additional five days at 20-25°C as per SOP 2.600.002 (Environmental Monitoring of the Clean-room Facility).
Upon reviewing the Environmental Monitoring results for the relevant testing dates, no microbial growth was observed on the ISO 5 BSC surface or settling 
plates, nor on the weekly active air and surface sampling plates from Cleanroom Suite 114 on the dates of testing, the dates prior and the subsequent 
testing dates. Additionally, both weekly active air sampling and weekly active surface sampling plates from both the week of testing and the week before 
testing, showed no microbial growth.

Although no microorganisms were identified from personnel or environmental monitoring samples, an adverse trend was observed. The lots that yielded 
failing results were tested by the same analyst within a span of a few days. Based on the historical analysis of samples from this client and the client’s 
sterilization process, it is highly unlikely that this number of lots would fail sterility testing in quick succession. Therefore, the possibility of an unidentified 
analyst-related error contributing to the failing results cannot be ruled out. These findings were discussed with the client, and the client will submit additional 
samples from the same lots for retesting. These additional samples were received under submission IDs ETX-260618-0132, ETX-260618-0133, ETX-
260618-0134, and ETX-260624-0149. 
261398

Tables 7 (see attached) presents the environmental monitoring results for the retest. The environmental monitoring (EM) plates were incubated for no less than 48 hours at 30-
35°C and no less than an additional five days at 20-25°C as per SOP 2.600.002 (Environmental Monitoring of the Clean-room Facility).

Upon review of the Environmental Monitoring (EM) results for the retest date, no microbial growth was detected on personnel glove plates or on the ISO 5 BSC 1988 surface and 
settling plates. Additionally, no microbial growth was observed on the active air sampling plates obtained both before and after testing. However, 11 CFU (ETX-260706-0305, OOS
-261553) were recovered from Room 142 during weekly active air sampling and identified as Micrococcus luteus, Staphylococcus haemolyticus, and Auricoccus indicus, all Gram 
(+) cocci. Additionally, 3 CFU (ETX-260706-0300) were recovered from Room 143, Section II, and identified as Micrococcus luteus and Staphylococcus capitis, both Gram (+) 
cocci. Weekly surface monitoring also detected 2 CFU (ETX-260706-0295) on the sink table in Room 142 (ISO 8); differential staining identified these organisms as Gram (+) rods.

Based on the EM data, the organisms recovered were isolated environmental events and did not demonstrate a pattern of contamination that would adversely affect sample 
processing. Therefore, the environmental monitoring results, combined with the controlled material transfer and disinfection practices, support the conclusion that the observed 
microbial recoveries had no significant impact on the processing conditions or the integrity of the test samples.

MICRO-SOP-5 - USP <71> / EP 2.6.1 Sterility Test
MICRO-SOP-9 - Cleaning and Disinfecting Procedure for Microbiology
MICRO-SOP-2 - Environmental Monitoring of the Clean Room Facility

Environmental monitoring data associated with Qiyue Chen's processing activities will be trended for 2026 to identify any recurring patterns or shifts that may 
indicate increased contamination risk. Further data analysis will be conducted to evaluate analyst-specific performance, including determination of the Out-of-
Specification (OOS) failure rate for component samples. This analysis will include a summary of the total number of samples processed, the number of samples 
processed within each batch, and the corresponding number of positive results to identify any trends requiring corrective action.

No laboratory errors were identified in the passing sterility test results reported under ETX-260618-0132, ETX-260618-0133, and ETX-260624-0149, or in the failing result reported 
under ETX-260618-0134 for the USP <71> / EP 2.6.1 Sterility Test.
The positive sample (ETX-260618-0134) was submitted for microbial identification under ETX-260706-0293. Differential staining revealed Gram (+) cocci, and subsequent 
determinative identification identified the organisms as Micrococcus luteus, Kocuria indica, and Dermacoccus nishinomiyaensis, all of which are Gram (+) cocci.

Since no contamination was detected from the personnel or processing environment during testing. These results indicate that neither analyst technique nor the testing 
environment was a likely source of the contamination, thereby providing no evidence of laboratory-related contamination contributing to the positive findings. In contrast, the failing 
results associated with ETX-260529-0274, ETX-260601-0310, and ETX-260605-0141 were most likely attributable to laboratory error, as the corresponding retests were performed 
without any identified laboratory deficiencies and yielded passing results.

Table 2 and Table 3 present the environmental monitoring results for sample ETX-260706-0599. 
Environmental monitoring (EM) plates were incubated for a minimum of 48 hours at 30–35°C, followed by no 
less than five additional days at 20–25°C, in accordance with SOP 2.600.002 (Environmental Monitoring of the 
Cleanroom Facility).

Review of the environmental monitoring data showed no microbial growth in personnel monitoring samples (left 
and right touch), ISO 5 surface sampling, or ISO 5 settling plates associated with both the processing analyst 
VV (Biological Safety Cabinet E001317) and the changeover analyst ELB (Biological Safety Cabinet E001937).

The microbial recoveries identified during environmental monitoring are not considered to have impacted the 
sterility test results. All product-contact activities, including processing and changeover, were performed within 
certified ISO 5 biological safety cabinets (BSC E001317 and BSC E001937), which provide a significantly 
higher level of environmental control than the ISO 7 and ISO 8 areas where the air recoveries were detected. 
Environmental monitoring performed on the date of testing demonstrated no microbial growth in personnel 
monitoring samples, ISO 5 surface samples, or ISO 5 settling plates associated with either processing or 
changeover activities. In addition, the cleanroom suites operate under a positive-pressure airflow design that 
directs air from the cleaner ISO 5/ISO 7 areas outward toward the ISO 7/ISO 8 anterooms, minimizing the 
potential for contamination migration from the lower-classification areas into the critical processing 
environments.

JEsqueda , 9/30/2025, 4:15:53 PM
Furthermore, the organisms recovered from the ISO 8 active air samples (Section II and Room 142) were 
identified as Gram-positive cocci, whereas the microorganisms detected in the ScanRDI test sample 
exhibited rod-shaped morphology. This morphological distinction indicates that at least a portion of the 
environmental monitoring recoveries were not consistent with the microorganisms detected in the sample.
Although rod-shaped organisms were recovered during environmental monitoring, these findings were 
limited to a single CFU recovered from the ISO 7 (CR145) and seventeen CFUs recovered from ISO 8 
(CR143) Section I. Importantly, these recoveries were confined to the ambient air of the surrounding lower-
classification areas and were not associated with the ISO 5 processing environment. In addition, no 
corresponding microbial growth was detected on personnel monitoring samples, ISO 5 surface samples, or 
settling plates. When considered in conjunction with the satisfactory cleaning and disinfection activities 
performed prior to processing, the absence of contamination in critical environmental monitoring locations, 
and the negative results obtained for all other samples processed on the same day, the available evidence 
supports the conclusion that the microbial growth detected in the ISO 7 and ISO 8 areas neither 
contributed to nor affected the positive ScanRDI result.
